Teams can let Claude click

20 November 2026 · Reading time: 4 minutes

Anthropic has opened its computer use beta to Claude's Team and Enterprise plans. Claude can see a user's screen and work in the desktop apps they allow.

Sapaude retells the story in its own words. The source is below. Publisher: Sapaude.

In three points

Three points, in this order: what the source shows, where that claim stops, and what to check next.

  1. Anthropic's release notes of November 20 list computer use (beta) for Team and Enterprise plans. Claude sees the screen and clicks and types in desktop apps a user approves. The rollout to organizations is gradual.
  2. It is off by default, and only an Owner or Primary Owner can turn it on. Anthropic warns there is no sandbox between Claude and the apps, and folder limits, including read-only folders, do not apply.
  3. It runs only in the new Claude experience: Claude Desktop on macOS 14 or later and Windows, or from the web and mobile when Computer access is on. Cowork tasks and Claude Code are excluded.

Computer use reaches Team and Enterprise

Anthropic has made computer use available in beta on Claude's Team and Enterprise plans, according to its release notes of November 20, 2026. The feature lets Claude see a user's screen and work in the desktop apps they allow, clicking and typing the way a person would. It is rolling out to organizations gradually.

Computer use works only in the new Claude experience, where the "Chat and Cowork unified" capability is on. That means Claude Desktop on macOS 14 or later and Windows, plus Claude on the web and Claude Mobile if the organization's Computer access setting is on and Claude Desktop is open on the computer. It does not work in tasks started with the separate Cowork option or in Claude Code.

Owners switch it on, users approve apps

The feature is off by default. According to Anthropic's setup article, only an Owner or Primary Owner can enable it, under Organization settings → Capabilities. On Team plans the switch covers every user. Enterprise plans can limit it by role. Each user then turns on "Enable computer use" in Claude Desktop and approves apps one by one. On a Mac, Claude Desktop needs the Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions.

Owners can also keep a block list, Anthropic's example is a password manager, or an allow list that denies every other app. Claude takes screenshots to find its way around. They are saved with the chat and can include personal or confidential information.

No sandbox, and the lists have limits

Anthropic is explicit about the risks. There is no sandbox between Claude and a user's applications, and content on the screen, such as web pages or emails, could cause Claude to take unintended actions. Through approved apps, Claude can open, change or delete files outside the folders a user has connected. "Read only" folder settings don't apply either.

The app lists don't cover everything. Claude can still read text copied from a denied app, and websites, browser extensions and apps inside a remote desktop are outside the lists. Turning the feature off or changing a list can take about an hour, sometimes longer, to reach each computer. Organizations with the HIPAA-ready configuration, Zero Data Retention for Claude Code, customer-managed encryption keys or FERPA/K-12 settings can't turn it on.

What admins and users should check

If the setting is missing, Anthropic says it either hasn't reached the organization yet or the organization can't have it. Admins should settle on a block or allow list before enabling the feature. An allow list cuts off users who aren't on the latest Claude Desktop until they update. Given Anthropic's warnings, users are best served starting in apps where a wrong click does little harm, and watching the screen while Claude works.

What you can do

Admins: read Anthropic's setup article before switching it on and decide on a block or allow list for apps. Users: ask an owner whether computer use is on for your role.

In the app, the same story is also told shorter and in more detail, matched to your level.
